subject: Sparse Data Structures for IRT models: V-Dem measurement model application.

messages.author: c54de5caf9d55f77
messages.subject: Sparse Data Structures for IRT models: V-Dem measurement model application.
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run the V-Dem measurement model using the code as given in the methodology document (link: https://v-dem.net/media/filer_public/67/30/6730d372-7952-4c41-ac15-cc3ad0111830/v-dem_working_paper_2015_21.pdf). The code below is effectively the same, but I have made some changes (my added code in yellow; the corresponding original code in orange), because I encounter a problem with my data's missing variables denoted as 'NA' (Stan does not support sparse data structures):

data {
  int<lower=2> K; // categories
  int<lower=0> J; // raters
  int<lower=0> N; // N country-years
  int<lower=0> C; // countries
  int<lower=1> M; // observations
  int<lower=1,upper=N> nn[M]; // country-year for observation M
  int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[M]; // rater for observation M
  int<lower=-1,upper=K> wdata[M];
  // int<lower=-1,upper=K> wdata[N,J]; // data
  int<lower=1,upper=C> cdata[J]; // j country indices
  real gsigmasq; // rater-level gamma variance around country-level gammas
  real gsigmasqc; // country-level gamma variance around world gammas
  // vector [N] mc;
}
parameters {
  real Z;
  // instead of vector[N] Z;
  ordered[K-1] gamma[J];
  vector[K-1] gamma_mu; // world-level cutpoints
  matrix[C,(K-1)] gamma_c; // country-level cuts, rows are countries
  real<lower=0> beta[J]; // reliability score
}
model{
  vector[K] p;
  real left;
  real right;
  Z ~ normal(0,1); // vague prior
  // Z[i] ~ normal(mc[i],1);
  gamma_mu ~ uniform(-2,2);
  for (c in 1:C) {
    gamma_c[c] ~ normal(gamma_mu,gsigmasqc); // row-access of gamma_c
  }
  for (j in 1:J) {
    gamma[j] ~ normal(gamma_c[cdata[j]],gsigmasq); // note row-access
    beta[j] ~ normal(1,1)T[0,]; // truncated so that > 0
    // for (i in 1:N) if (wdata[i,j] != -1) {
      for (m in 1:M) if (wdata[m] != -1) {
        left <- 0;
        for (k in 1:(K-1)) {
          right <- left;
          left <- Phi_approx(gamma[j,k]-Z*beta[j]); // fast approximation to Phi
          p[k] <- left - right;
        }
        p[K] <- 1.0 - left;
        wdata[m] ~ categorical(p);
        // wdata[i,j] ~ categorical(p);
      }
    }
  }

The error message I get is the following:

Error in FUN(c("K", "J", "N", "C", "wdata", "cdata", "gsigmasq", "gsigmasqc" : 
  Stan does not support NA (in wdata) in data
failed to preprocess the data; sampling not done

I have made the aforementioned changes consulting the Stan manual and specifically section 13.1, p. 143, where a similar situation is described. I still get the error message above (in red). I do not see why the problem is not resolved and still Stan 'sees' the NA values. Can anyone help, please?

Panos

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sparse Data Structures for IRT models: V-Dem measurement model application.
parts:
You can't pass NA values into Stan. It can
only see them if you pass them in, so check your
inputs carefully.

There's a chapter in the manual for dealing with
missing data --- it's flexible in Stan, but the
syntax is much clunkier than BUGS or JAGS.

- Bob
